---
title: "as.numeric() on a factor returns the codes"
ref: FCT-01
categories: [Factors]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'as.numeric(factor("2024"))'
reponse: '1'
attendu: "`2024 2026 2024`"
versions: "All, more common before R 4.0 when read.csv() created factors"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
year <- factor(c("2024", "2026", "2024"))
as.numeric(year)
```
:::

## Why

A factor is an integer vector paired with a table of levels. `as.numeric()` reads the integers, that is the position of each value among the sorted levels, not the text you see printed.

Before R 4.0, `read.csv()` turned text columns into factors by default. A badly read column of years would then yield "years" 1, 2 and 1, plausible enough inside a model.

## The remedy

Go back through the text, or index the levels.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
as.numeric(as.character(year))
as.numeric(levels(year))[year]
```
:::
